\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes.} One row per decision; a jurisdiction that paused and later cancelled appears twice, and the same decision reported by several sources appears once. \textit{Towns} are New England towns and township governments (Census county subdivisions), which fall outside the Census place universe. Every decision was confirmed against a source document (council minutes, a government release, or local news) on October 26, 2026. Sources: the DeFlock ``wins'' register, a Nexis Uni search of local news, and a search for decisions those two had not yet recorded: every entry of two national trackers (deflocktheusa.com, whoapprovedthis.org) checked against local sources, plus state-by-state searches of local news and council records. ``Followed a state action'': decisions made because of a state law, order, or request --- chiefly Florida agencies acting on the state Department of Transportation's revocation of ALPR permits on state roads (August 31, 2026), Texas agencies acting on the governor's pause of state grant funding, and Washington agencies complying with SB 6002; also Vermont's ALPR statute and the Connecticut governor's pause request. Partial actions (only some cameras, only new installations, only state-road cameras) are counted as decisions. Reasons are as stated by the deciding body or reported in coverage; ``privacy'' includes general surveillance concerns. States with eight or more decisions: FL (100), WI (60), MA (47), TX (40), VA (35), WA (33), CA (28), MI (26), OH (24), CO (22), MN (20), NY (20), NC (18), AZ (15), MO (14), TN (14), IL (13), OR (13), AR (12), KY (12), CT (11), IN (10), RI (9), ME (8).
\end{tablenotes}
